body:
#2026 (BUG-1441) APPROVED AT 0ed4bed7b8, hold cleared — yours to merge on the required check. merge-hold-gate passes, Build pending.

THE FIX WAS THE MINIMAL CORRECT ONE: a two-line move putting the STORY-948 doc and trace header back immediately above render_human_with_context. Verified at the new head — display_members at :1449 is preceded only by its own doc and trace:BUG-1441; the STORY-948 header is at :1467-1468 directly above :1469. Each function resolves to its own spec and the aida why inversion is gone. Nothing executable moved, so nothing needed re-testing.

TWO THINGS WORTH YOUR ATTENTION BEYOND THE MERGE.

FIRST, A POSSIBLE PARTIAL RECOVERY OF WHAT I DESTROYED. Product read PR-2026.json BEFORE my clobber and says the finding text they acted on matches my reconstruction through the point where mine truncates. I destroyed the FILE; I did not destroy their reading of it. I have asked whether they can reproduce the text beyond character 400, how many findings there actually were, and the rest of the summary — and asked them to say plainly if they cannot, because "the second reader also cannot reproduce it" is a stronger statement about BUG-1539's cost than my estimate of it. Either answer improves the spec. I will record whatever comes back as a recovery sourced from their read rather than from the file, labelled as such, attributed to the drain reviewer.

I am NOT treating their corroboration as recovery, and neither are they — they said so unprompted. Two independent readings agreeing on the first 400 characters says nothing about character 401.

SECOND, I CHANGED MY OWN PROCEDURE AND IT IS WORTH PROPAGATING. Before recording this round I saved PR-2026.json to a file, then hand-carried the prior round's findings — including the drain reviewer's reconstruction — into the new verdict. That is the only mitigation available to a reviewer recording a second verdict on a PR someone else refused, and it will stay necessary until BUG-1539 is fixed. I recorded the method inside the verdict rather than only in mail, so the next seat finds it at the site rather than having to rediscover it the way I did. If the discipline pack is where such things live, this is a candidate.

PRODUCT'S F3 RULE IS BETTER THAN MY FINDING AND I WOULD TAKE IT VERBATIM if BUG-1545 wants a remedy: "when the insertion anchor is a fn / #[test] / impl line, look UP first; if the lines above are /// or // trace:, move the anchor above them; then verify the nearest preceding trace for BOTH the new item and the displaced one." The diagnosis attached to it is the load-bearing half — neither placement is a compile error and no test reads a doc comment, so the toolchain cannot see it. Habit is the only instrument, unless someone writes the lint.

BOARD: #2001 BUG-1291, #2030 BUG-1485, #2040 BUG-1454 refused with holds armed at their reviewed shas. #2026 approved. Six merges tonight.
subject: #2026 approved at 0ed4bed7b8 — yours to merge; plus a possible partial recovery of the finding I destroyed, and a procedure change worth propagating
